evidence: Pre-fix judge_report ran judge_validate once as a discarded-output gate and again on the next line purely to scrape the percentage, so the entire held set was scored twice and the second run was assumed to reproduce the first; e4e8701 replaced both with one capture (vout=$(judge_validate "$judge" 2>&1); vrc=$?), verified in lib.sh at that ref.
guidance_note: When a caller needs both a status and a number the callee already computed, make the callee hand back both from one invocation instead of calling it twice for two halves of the same result.

evidence: The pre-fix line piped a SECOND judge_validate run through grep -o '= [0-9]*%' with no failure path, so any change to the judge_log wording or any failure of that run would print the tag 'validated (agreement  >= bar 80%)' with a hole where the number belongs; the post-fix code reads the percentage from the single captured output with a '?' fallback and distinguishes rc>=2 as infra error.
guidance_note: Read a value out of a call's captured output rather than re-invoking it and scraping its log, and give the extraction an explicit fallback so a miss prints visibly instead of as an empty gap.

evidence: Third of three round-0 comments on the same defect: the agreement percentage existed only inside judge_validate's log text, so judge_report had to re-run the function and parse prose to recover a number the function had already computed. One fix in e4e8701 closed all three.

judge.sh scored with grep -qF (substring) while its own header said 'contains every line of the reference', so 'UNAPPROVED' satisfies the reference line 'APPROVED'; the reviewer offered either grep -qxF or a doc correction, and the agent took the doc option, which is right here because the sample judge's blind spots are the point of the tier.
guidance_note: Name the matching mode (substring vs whole-line) in the comment beside any grep-based contract; 'contains every line' reads as line-exact and the code was not.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: JUDGE_HERE is present in lib.sh at the original commit 166c81f (read via the contents API) and e4e8701 touched only judge_report and judge.sh, so the dead variable predates the named fix and round 0 simply missed it. It is genuinely unreferenced - zero hits across lib.sh's three callers (score-judge.sh, validate-judge.sh, verify-judge.sh).
guidance_note: Do not paste the boilerplate HERE=$(cd "$(dirname ...)") line into a library that never resolves a path from it.

evidence: The original 166c81f header attributed case-4 only to a human-label disagreement; F4's fix in e4e8701 rewrote it so the substring looseness and case-4 sat in one sentence ('a real blind spot - and that is the point ... on held case-4 it passes an artifact a human labelled fail'), yet case-4/output.txt is exactly 'APPROVED' against reference 'APPROVED' - an exact match that exercises no substring path. The round-2 text separates the two blind spots explicitly.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites an explanatory comment, re-read the example the comment cites and confirm it still demonstrates the claim the new wording makes.

narrative: Round 0 raised one real defect (judge_report re-running the whole held set to scrape a percentage out of its own log) three times as F1/F2/F3, plus a genuine doc-vs-code mismatch in the sample judge. The single fix in e4e8701 was clean and closed all three. Round 1 cost a round for two reasons: a dead JUDGE_HERE that had been in the original commit and was missed first time, and a comment that F4's own fix had made untrue by welding the substring blind spot onto case-4, whose output is an exact match. Only the second is fix-caused; the first would have forced the same extra round anyway, so no round is strictly avoidable.
guidance_observations: The reviewer emitted three separate threads for one double-invocation defect, which triples the agent's reply cost without adding information.
The one fix-caused finding in this PR was a comment, not code - rewriting an explanation is where this agent's fixes drift.

evidence: The DEPENDENCY_DIFF paragraph is verbatim in the installer template, not hand-pasted into the artifact: the same block ('a deliberate universal default baked into the template ... Do not reconverge to a barer default') sits in agent-code-review-setup/install.sh in the dotfiles repo and emits exactly the lines at code-review.yml:55-63 in d734b0c. The reviewer's premise - that a re-run of install.sh would drop the comment - is the opposite of the truth.
guidance_note: When a generated file's template lives outside the repo, say where in the file's own header, so a reviewer scoped to this repo cannot read generated content as a local hand edit.

narrative: One finding, and the reviewer was wrong on a fact it could not see: the review is scoped to this repo and the installer template lives in another one, so it read a generated comment block as a hand edit and inferred a one-source-of-truth violation that does not exist. The agent pushed back with the template path and line range and made no change, which is correct. The pushback cost no extra round.
guidance_observations: Review scope that stops at the repo boundary produces confident findings about provenance; a one-line pointer in the generated header is the cheap defense.
This is the batch's only pushback and it was well-evidenced - the agent named the file and lines rather than asserting the premise was wrong.

evidence: The test stat-ed $TMPDIR/laws-medium-lock/S1 and named the 'main' slot, duplicating LOCK_ROOT and the slot default defined in skill-router.sh; the agent declined the reviewer's derive-the-constant fix (which keeps the structural coupling) and instead proved the same two facts through the guard's own output, and c27b5cb touched only the test file (+8-5).
guidance_note: Assert a hook's contract through its stdout rather than by stat-ing the files it writes - a filesystem probe in a test is a second definition of the layout.

evidence: Premise holds: 'mkdir -p ... && printf > "$lock"' followed by an unconditional exit 0 reports allow with no lock written, so the next different medium looks like a first load. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive - c27b5cb changed only skill-router.test.sh (+8-5 per the commits API), so this code came from the original b50c47e and round 0 missed it.
guidance_note: Check the one external write a guard performs as you write it: an && chain followed by an unconditional exit 0 announces a success it never verified.

evidence: Same defect and same line as F2, raised twice in round 1 with the same suggested fix; one push (b4b0233) closed both. Flag is a false positive for the same reason: c27b5cb touched only the test file, so the unchecked lock write predates it.

sanitize()'s class 'A-Za-z0-9._-' keeps the dot while the comment directly above claims the tr stops 'a slash or dot', and session-start runs rm -rf "$(lock_dir_for "$sid")", so a '..' id would resolve to LOCK_ROOT's parent - read in skill-router.sh at b4b0233. Flag is a false positive: b4b0233 changed only the lock-write block (+10-2), sanitize() dates from b50c47e.
guidance_note: Pick a sanitizing character class from what the ids legitimately contain, and read the class against the comment that claims what it excludes.

evidence: The lock is created by reading [ -f "$lock" ] and then writing, so two parallel Skill loads in one slot can both see it empty and the later write wins, erasing the first recorded medium; the agent made creation atomic with ( set -o noclobber; printf > "$lock" ) and routed the losing branch back into the comparison. Flag is a false positive: the check-then-write shape came from b50c47e and b4b0233 only wrapped the write in an if.
guidance_note: Make a first-writer-wins lock atomic at creation with set -o noclobber instead of check-then-write, and send the loser back through the comparison rather than the failure path.

evidence: The reviewer's mechanism is overstated and the agent said so correctly: grep is line-oriented but every real pretty-printer emits "session_id": "uuid" on one line, so the silent-empty failure needs a formatter that splits key from value and none does. The undocumented single-line assumption is still real, and the agent applied the reviewer's own fix (INPUT=$(cat | tr -d "\n")), so the thread is a correct split answer. Flag is a false positive: json_field came from b50c47e.
guidance_note: Normalize a parser's input at the read, or state the shape assumption where the parser is defined, so the assumption is not carried only by the test payloads.

evidence: The router resets the lock on startup|clear|fork and preserves it on resume|compact, but only compact had a case, so moving resume into the reset arm would have passed the suite green; the agent added the symmetric resume case. Flag is a false positive: b4b0233 added only the read-only-TMPDIR case, and both the branch and the test file are from b50c47e.
guidance_note: When a branch enumerates two lists of sources, pin one case from each list - a single case proves only the arm it sits in.

narrative: Four rounds, seven findings, and not one of them was caused by an earlier fix: every later-round finding sits in code the original commit b50c47e introduced, in regions the fix commits either did not touch (sanitize, json_field, the test's source coverage) or only wrapped (the lock write). The commits API settles this - c27b5cb is test-only and b4b0233 is +10-2 in the router. The cost here is review incompleteness compounded by the agent not sweeping its own new hook script against the laws its header already cites: an unchecked external write, a check-then-write race, and a comment contradicting its own character class all shipped in the first push. The agent's judgment was good throughout - it upgraded F1's fix from dedup to behavioral assertions and correctly narrowed F6's overstated premise while still hardening.
guidance_observations: Three of the four rounds existed to find defects in a single new 125-line script; a self-review pass applying no-silent-failure and the traversal/race checks to every write in a new file would have collapsed them.
The reviewer raised F2 and F3 as separate threads for one line, and duplicate threads are a recurring tax in this repo's reviews.
Every fix commit here drew a fresh crop of findings in untouched neighbouring code, which means round count tracks reviewer sampling as much as it tracks agent quality.

evidence: plugin.json's description still advertised 'code / prose / prompt / ticket' while skills/ticket was disabled on disk and this same PR removed ticket from ROUTE_TEXT, so the manifest promised routing the plugin no longer performs; fixed in b844a8c.
guidance_note: When a medium or feature is removed from the routing surface, grep the manifest and its description for the name in the same commit rather than leaving the advertisement behind.

evidence: The discriminators the reviewer wants restored are already in the skills' own frontmatter at b844a8c - laws:prompt's description reads 'task prompts, subagent instructions ... skill bodies, hook text' and laws:prose's says 'Do not apply to code or to text another LLM will consume' - and the harness injects those descriptions into every session's available-skills listing, so the prose-vs-prompt edge case the reviewer names is resolved in-context without a second copy in ROUTE_TEXT.
guidance_note: State in the route text's comment that the medium discriminators live in the skill descriptions, so a reviewer reads the removal as deduplication rather than as lost information.

narrative: Two findings, cleanly split: a genuinely stale manifest description that the agent fixed, and a request to restore text this PR deliberately removed, which the agent refused with a checkable reason. The pushback verifies - the skill frontmatter descriptions carry the exact discriminators the reviewer listed, and they are in context in every session, so restoring them to ROUTE_TEXT would have re-created two routing surfaces that drift. Round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: A reviewer with no model of what the harness injects will read deliberate deduplication as information loss; naming the other source in a comment is what prevents it.
The agent's pushback named the canonical location and the specific edge case the reviewer cited, which is why it held.

evidence: The duplicate-member and smuggled-arm failure arms named the real task laws-scripts-parse and asserted only that something aborted, so renaming that task would make the arm die with 'suite names a task that does not exist' and still pass green; the fix pointed SUITE_TASKS_ROOT at a fabricated root with a file://-backed dummy task and added an expected-error column so each arm asserts its own violation.
guidance_note: A failure-arm test must assert which failure fired and build its own fixture; borrowing a real inventory entry makes the arm pass on the wrong abort.

evidence: cdbc132 added go-template-multi-regression/check.sh and go-template-stub-reimpl/check.sh as +39-0 each and they were byte-identical; c3b026a replaced both with 4-line wrappers over evals/tasks/criteria/compound-gates.sh, so the gate set now has one definition.
guidance_note: Extract a criterion at the moment the second task copies it verbatim - the copy, not the third instance, is the point where drift becomes possible.

evidence: run-suite.sh passed an unvalidated $reps into for ((i = 1; i <= reps; i++)) after compare_repeated had already rejected it, so a garbage reps printed a grid of empty cells with no '!' markers while exiting 1; the agent refused to copy compare/lib.sh's case pattern and hoisted the rule into cmp_reps_validate called by both. Flag is a false positive: run-suite.sh was added in cdbc132 and untouched by c3b026a.
guidance_note: Validate a CLI's numeric argument at the entry point before any directory or run is created, not only inside the subshell that consumes it.

evidence: compound-gates.sh was created by the F2 extraction in c3b026a. The pre-fix check.sh sourced its OWN neighbouring manifest (. "$HERE/manifest.sh", read at cdbc132), which always exists; the extraction turned that path into a caller-supplied $task_dir, making a missing manifest genuinely reachable, and under set -e the source's exit 1 is the FAIL verdict code against the file's own stated 0/1/2 contract.
guidance_note: When a refactor turns a fixed neighbouring path into a parameter, add the existence and sourcing guards the fixed path made unnecessary - the new argument is a new failure mode.

narrative: Round 0 found two real things: failure arms that could pass on the wrong abort, and a byte-identical criterion in two tasks. Both fixes were sound, and the arms fix went beyond what was asked by adding per-arm expected errors. Round 1's two findings split - the reps validation gap was pre-existing in run-suite.sh and untouched by the fix commit, while the compound-gates exit-code gap is genuinely a product of the extraction, which converted a guaranteed sibling path into a caller argument without adding the guard that change requires. Round 1 would have happened for the reps finding regardless, so no round is strictly avoidable.
guidance_observations: The one fix-caused finding in this PR came from a de-duplication refactor changing a path's provenance - extraction moves reachability, and the reachability check has to move with it.
The agent twice chose a better fix shape than the reviewer proposed (hermetic fixture root, hoisted validator) and said why, which is the pattern worth keeping.

evidence: The stub-gutting loop and the test-deletion loop each enumerate all seven helpers while the leftover grep listed five, omitting standalone 'wrap' and 'initials', so a fixture exercising those two would survive the sweep as visible coverage and quietly defeat the task's headroom; 45961a7 extended the pattern with a word-bounded wrap and verified a clean run against a fresh clone of the pinned commit.
guidance_note: When one script writes the same list of names three times, derive the later uses from the array the first loop iterates instead of retyping a subset into a regex.

evidence: The premise holds - '|| true' maps grep rc>1 onto the empty-leftover shape the guard reads as clean - but the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: the same '2>/dev/null || true' is visible in F1's round-0 diff hunk at line 134, so it predates 45961a7. The fix nonetheless rewrote that exact expression and left the swallow in place, which is why this round happened.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites a line, hold the whole expression to the file's own stated laws - the guard's grep was mapping an infra failure onto its success shape in the same expression the pattern was being edited.

narrative: One finding per round, both real, both about the same expression. Round 0 caught a drift-guard regex covering five of seven gutted helpers; the fix rewrote that grep line and verified it against the pinned commit. Round 1 then flagged the '2>/dev/null || true' on the very same line, which had been there since round 0 - so this is not a bug introduced by the fix, but it is a round the agent bought by editing an expression without auditing the rest of it. That makes round 1, and therefore the round-2 confirmation, avoidable in the sense that matters to this audit even though caused_by is null.
guidance_observations: The cheapest round saved in this PR was a re-read of the single line being edited, not a broader sweep.
Both fixes were empirically verified against a fresh clone of the pinned commit, and neither introduced a follow-on finding - verification of the fix itself is not this repo's weak point.
